[Resource Allocation](06_resource_allocation.qmd) ended with the event log recording who was sent to each call, or that nobody was. This chapter covers what reads that log afterwards.

## What it is {#sec-trial-results-and-historic-comparison-what-it-is}

Three classes in `air_ambulance_des/` turn files on disk into numbers and Plotly figures. [`SimulationInputs`](../../reference/class_simulation_inputs.SimulationInputs.qmd) loads the parameters, rota, servicing and callsign files that the run used. [`TrialResults`](../../reference/class_simulation_trial_results.TrialResults.qmd) takes the combined event log (`data/run_results.csv`, see [Simulation Runs and Replications](02_simulation_runs_and_replications.qmd)) and does all its derivation in the constructor. `HistoricResults` loads the aggregated files in `historical_data/` plus a pre-computed simulated baseline that uses historic rotas. All three are wrapped by `graceful_methods`, which swallows exceptions.

Callers can rely on this much, and no more: construct `TrialResults(...)` once with the run's `run_results` frame and every derived DataFrame attribute exists afterwards (`call_df`, `utilisation_df_overall`, `missed_jobs_per_run_care_cat_summary`, and so on), possibly as `None` if its step failed (see `graceful_methods` below). Plot methods return a Plotly figure or `None`. The `PLOT_*`, `get_*` and `display_*` methods read from those attributes. The main caller is the results page in `app/model.py`, which uses it to show missed jobs, utilisation and comparisons with history (@fig-trial-results-flow). Nothing here feeds back into the simulation.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-trial-results-flow
%%| fig-cap: "Files in, objects in the middle, figures out"
flowchart LR
  RR[data/run_results.csv] --> TR[TrialResults]
  RP[data/run_params_used.csv<br>actual_data rota files] --> SI[SimulationInputs]
  SI --> TR
  DA[data/daily_availability.csv] --> TR
  HD[historical_data/ and<br>tests/rotas_historic] --> HR[HistoricResults]
  HR -->|passed into plot methods| TR
  TR --> APP[app/model.py tabs and report]
  HR --> APP
```

The use case I will follow throughout is the "Missed Jobs" and utilisation panels: what fraction of calls found no resource (for example, `get_perc_unattended_string_normalised` returns a string such as `"2 of 480 (< 0.1%)"` when the fraction is under 1%), and how busy each callsign was compared with history.

## How it works {#sec-trial-results-and-historic-comparison-how-it-works}

### The error-swallowing decorator

Everything below sits under `graceful_methods`, so read this first.

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/_processing_functions.py" start-line=40 end-line=74 filename="air_ambulance_des/_processing_functions.py:40-74" code-line-style="hi:5-6,focus:9-21" include-hash="b33d253be733"}
```

It rebinds every callable in `cls.__dict__` whose name does not start with `__`. Any exception becomes either `st.error(...)` (if `streamlit.runtime.exists()`) or a `print`, and the method returns `None`. Three consequences that matter when you debug:

- `__init__` is **not** wrapped (it starts with `__`), but every method it calls is. A failing step in a constructor therefore leaves the attribute at its `None` placeholder and carries on.
- The wrapper is not decorated with `functools.wraps`, so wrapped methods lose their docstrings and `__name__` (the name in the message comes from the closure variable `fn`).
- There is no traceback in this variant. The sibling `graceful` function in the same file does print one, but it is not applied to these classes.

### SimulationInputs

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_inputs.py" start-line=5 end-line=22 filename="air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_inputs.py:5-22" code-line-style="hi:10-13" include-hash="8d4a36a4195a"}
```

It is a bag of five DataFrames. Note the split: the parameters and `service_dates.csv` come from `data_folder_path` (outputs of the run), whereas the rota, callsign lookup and rota month bounds come from `actual_data_folder_path` (inputs, see [Streamlit App and Scenario Parameters](01_streamlit_app_and_scenario_parameters.qmd)). Because `__init__` is unwrapped, a missing file raises `FileNotFoundError` straight out.

### TrialResults: the constructor is the pipeline

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py" start-line=197 end-line=231 filename="air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py:197-231" code-line-style="focus:2-11" include-hash="e419bac16006"}
```

The order matters because each step reads attributes set by an earlier one. `make_job_count_df` needs `enhance_run_results`; `make_utilisation_model_dataframe` needs `total_avail_minutes` from `calculate_available_hours`. Nothing enforces this.

`make_job_count_df` collapses the event log to one row per patient per run. Since `hems_result`, `outcome`, `vehicle_type`, `callsign` and `registration` are only filled on later events (see [Calls and Patient Journeys](04_calls_and_patient_journeys.qmd)), it back-fills them within each `(P_ID, run_number)` group and then keeps only the `arrival` row:

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py" start-line=621 end-line=631 filename="air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py:621-631" code-line-style="hi:7-8" include-hash="ff3c4121c8b9"}
```

A call with no resource has no callsign anywhere in its rows, so the back-fill leaves NaN. `get_UNATTENDED_calls_per_run` relies on that, and the TODO above flags the open question of what to do with these NaNs. Note the side effect: `call_df` is written to `data/call_df.csv`, a path relative to the current working directory.

### Theoretical available hours: the utilisation denominator

Utilisation is time in use divided by time the resource was rostered. `calculate_available_hours` builds the denominator by walking every day from `warm_up_end_date` to `sim_end_date` and adding each rota line's minutes, using the summer or winter columns depending on the month bounds from `rota_start_end_months.csv`.

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py" start-line=345 end-line=368 filename="air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py:345-368" dedent=8 code-line-style="focus:7-16" include-hash="f4411acb06fa"}
```

An overnight shift (start after end) credits `24 - start` hours to today and `end` hours to the next day, which is why the loop indexes `date_idx + 1`. The final day's overnight spill is dropped. Equal start and end hours credit zero minutes.

The docstring says servicing is taken into account, and `service_df` is loaded and merged with the callsign lookup, but a search of the method finds no later use of it: the minutes are computed from the rota alone. Treat the denominator as "rostered minutes", not "rostered minus servicing".

The method then writes three files as side effects (`data/daily_availability.csv`, `data/monthly_availability.csv`, `data/daily_availability_summary.csv`), again relative to the working directory.

### Utilisation

`make_utilisation_model_dataframe` pivots the `resource_use` and `resource_use_end` events to one row per use, fills missing ends with the sim end date and missing starts with the warm-up end, then sums minutes per callsign.

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py" start-line=563 end-line=580 filename="air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py:563-580" dedent=8 code-line-style="hi:5-7,hi:12-14" include-hash="f0ef853a79a7"}
```

Per-run durations are summed over runs, divided by `n_runs`, then divided by the single-run availability. The code comment elsewhere says availability is assumed identical across runs, which holds because the rota is fixed for a trial.

### Missed jobs

Missed jobs are defined by `event_type == "resource_request_outcome"` rows whose `time_type` is `"No Resource Available"`. The normalised string annualises both counts using `sim_duration_days`:

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py" start-line=2304 end-line=2322 filename="air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py:2304-2322" dedent=8 code-line-style="focus:10-19" include-hash="cd8fdf7a3c83"}
```

`get_missed_call_df` does the same grouped by `care_cat` and `time_type`, recoding `REG` with `heli_benefit == "y"` to `"REG - Helicopter Benefit"`, and produces the per-run breakdown and the min/mean/max summary the plots use. There is also a second, older route, `get_UNATTENDED_calls_per_run`, that counts NaN callsigns instead. The two should agree but are computed from different columns.

### Comparing with history

`HistoricResults.__init__` is a long run of "set `None`, then call the loader" pairs, each loader a `pd.read_csv` on `historical_data/<name>.csv` or `historical_data/calculated/<name>.csv`. The `calculated/` files are the simulated baseline produced by the offline pipeline in [Distribution Fitting](08_distribution_fitting.qmd). The constructor comment explains the purpose: some quantities (such as patients who would have benefited from enhanced care but did not get it) cannot be observed, so they are simulated with historic rotas.

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/class_historic_results.py" start-line=73 end-line=94 filename="air_ambulance_des/class_historic_results.py:73-94" code-line-style="hi:4-5,hi:15-17" include-hash="e8ebe9733c8c"}
```

`TrialResults` never imports `HistoricResults`. The historical object is passed into the plot method that needs it, which then reaches into its attributes:

```{.python include="../../../air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py" start-line=2649 end-line=2660 filename="air_ambulance_des/class_simulation_trial_results.py:2649-2660" dedent=8 code-line-style="hi:3-5" include-hash="63ee01631366"}
```

`PLOT_SIMULATION_utilisation_summary` draws the simulated bars, then, for each callsign that also appears in `historical_utilisation_df_summary`, overlays a min-to-max rectangle and a dotted mean line. That summary is built in `make_RWC_utilisation_dataframe` (RWC is not expanded anywhere in the code; it presumably means "real-world comparison", i.e. built from historic data), which recomputes theoretical availability per month from the historic rota files in the same way as above.

The app wires all of this together like so:

```{.python include="../../../app/model.py" start-line=245 end-line=275 filename="app/model.py:245-275" dedent=8 code-line-style="hi:21-26" include-hash="9c7ccd931a98"}
```

## Extending this {#sec-trial-results-and-historic-comparison-extending-this}

**Add a metric or plot.** Add a method to `TrialResults` (it is wrapped automatically, since the decorator walks `cls.__dict__`). If it needs a derived table, build it in a `make_*`/`get_*` method and call that from the constructor sequence at lines 197-231, after anything it reads. Name plot methods `PLOT_*` and text/Streamlit helpers `display_*` or `get_*` to match the convention. Then call it from the relevant tab in `app/model.py`.

**Add a historical comparison.** Add a `get_historical_<name>` loader to `HistoricResults`, initialise the attribute to `None` in `__init__` just before calling it, and make sure the CSV is written by `DistributionFitUtils` (the `historical_*` methods, see [Distribution Fitting](08_distribution_fitting.qmd)). If you add a `calculated/` file it must also be produced by `run_sim_on_historical_params`. Pass the `HistoricResults` instance into your plot method as the existing plots do.

**Add an input file to SimulationInputs.** Add the path and `pd.read_csv` in `__init__`, and make sure whichever stage writes it (the run in [Simulation Runs and Replications](02_simulation_runs_and_replications.qmd) or the setup page) does so before the results page runs.

**Change what counts as a missed job.** The definition is repeated: `get_perc_unattended_string`, `get_perc_unattended_string_normalised`, `get_missed_call_df`, `get_UNATTENDED_calls_per_run` and the historical equivalents all filter independently. Change them together, and check the event strings against those emitted in [Resource Allocation](06_resource_allocation.qmd).

**Tests.** This abstraction has no tests. None of `tests/` imports `TrialResults`, `HistoricResults` or `SimulationInputs`. The repo documents `pytest` from the project root (and `pytest -m <marker>` for subsets; see `tests/README.md`), which will at least confirm the simulation still produces an event log these classes can read, but it will not exercise this code. For a change here, build a small `run_results` DataFrame by hand, construct `TrialResults` in a script run from the repo root, and check the derived attributes. The working directory matters because of the relative `data/` paths.

## Sharp edges {#sec-trial-results-and-historic-comparison-sharp-edges}

- **Silent `None`.** Any exception in a wrapped method yields `None` plus a printed message (or a Streamlit error box). `get_AVERAGE_calls_per_run` is a live example: it calls `self.get_calls_per_run(self.call_df)`, but `get_calls_per_run` takes no argument, so the call raises `TypeError` and the method always returns `None`.
- **Constructor continues after failures.** Because `__init__` calls wrapped methods, a failure in, say, `calculate_available_hours` leaves `total_avail_minutes` as `None` and the utilisation step then fails in turn. The first printed message is the real cause.
- **Working-directory coupling.** `TrialResults` writes `data/call_df.csv`, `data/daily_availability.csv`, `data/monthly_availability.csv` and `data/daily_availability_summary.csv`. `HistoricResults` writes `historical_data/calculated/theoretical_availability_historical.csv`. All are relative paths, so the code only works when started from the repo root (as the app is).
- **Stale availability input.** `app/model.py` reads `data/daily_availability.csv` and passes it in as `daily_availability_data`, but `calculate_available_hours` later in the constructor overwrites that same file. The `daily_availability_df` used by `PLOT_daily_availability` therefore comes from whatever was on disk before this run, which may be a previous scenario's. This follows from the call order and is not documented.
- **Hard-coded summer in the historic path.** In `HistoricResults.make_RWC_utilisation_dataframe`, the nested `is_summer` ignores its argument, reads `current_date` from the enclosing loop, and hard-codes months 4 to 9 (`class_historic_results.py:324-325`). `TrialResults` instead takes the bounds from `rota_start_end_months.csv`. If you change the summer months, the simulated side follows and the historic side does not.
- **Mismatched message.** In `get_perc_unattended_string` (`class_simulation_trial_results.py:2278-2279`) and `get_perc_unattended_string_normalised` (`:2324-2327`), the test `< 0.01` (1%) prints "(< 0.1%)". The string should read "(< 1%)".
- **Vehicle-grouping assumption.** `make_SIMULATION_utilisation_headline_figure` classes a callsign group with one member as "solo car" and with two as "helicopter backup car", and says in a comment that this may not hold forever.
- **Cost.** `calculate_available_hours` and its historic twin loop over days times rota rows with `.loc` writes. Long simulations with many rota lines are slow, and this runs on every results-page build.
- **Dependence on the Streamlit runtime.** `_processing_functions.py` imports `streamlit` at module level, so even headless use of these classes needs it installed.

## Design notes {#sec-trial-results-and-historic-comparison-design-notes}

**Documented.**

- Refactor to class-based results: commit `8b393b5` (2025-10-07) is described as a major interim refactor to `TrialResults` and `HistoricResults`. Commit `0704f3d` restored the first page of output and five follow-ups restored the remaining plots one tab at a time. Commit `7ae9c47` improved the layout and clarity of the historic class.
- Daily availability data flow: commit `3039d72` changed how daily availability data enters the app and `TrialResults`, and `81982cc` made sure it is assigned to a class attribute.
- Streamlit Cloud indexing bug: commits `cfa31e0` and `a7684b9`.

**Inferred.** The state of the code suggests the refactor is unfinished. Markers say "NOT YET CONVERTED TO OO" (line 2407) and "convert to use historical class" (line 2741), and a few methods take `historical_results_obj` or `historical_data_class` as an argument instead of using `self.historical_data`. The decorator presumably exists so that one broken plot cannot take down a results page with a dozen tabs; the cost is the silent `None` behaviour above. Computing everything in `__init__` presumably trades construction time for cheap plot calls, since Streamlit reruns the script on every interaction. No commit or doc states either reason.

## Limitations and open questions {#sec-trial-results-and-historic-comparison-limitations}

::: {.callout-note title="Why the model makes simplifying assumptions"}
Every simulation model rests on assumptions and simplifications, and it has to. No model can be a perfect copy of reality. Adding ever more detail does not fix that, and can make things worse: each extra detail is one more thing to get wrong, so an over-complicated model can drift further from reality, not closer. Judge the items below, and any change you are tempted to make, against whether the assumption is reasonable for the questions asked of the model. Closing every gap with reality is not the aim, and extra fidelity can add more error than it removes.
:::

TODO markers in `class_simulation_trial_results.py`:

- Line 471 (repeated near the end of the file): add a check that missing resource-use start/end times are only back-filled for calls at the edges of the model, not for errors elsewhere.
- Line 621: decide what to do with columns that remain NA after back-filling.
- Lines 931 and 1180: pull historical data from the historical class rather than elsewhere.
- Line 2226: confirm the difference between `run_results` and `event_log_df`.
- Line 2407: a block of plot code not yet converted to the object-oriented layout.
- Line 2741: convert to use the historical class.

Issues open as of 2026-10-19: [#217](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/DAA_DES/issues/217) (utilisation breakdown plot breaks when one helicopter/car pairing is removed), [#215](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/DAA_DES/issues/215) (car utilisation metrics break when one car is removed), [#176](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/DAA_DES/issues/176) (no formal tests for the utilisation denominator), [#165](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/DAA_DES/issues/165) (discrepancies between metrics and historical data) and [#244](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/DAA_DES/issues/244) (a copyable summary table of key metrics).

See the [issue tracker](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/DAA_DES/issues) for the current state.
